answer.company: Allbirds (now reportedly renamed Smartbird; Nasdaq: BIRD)

signals.summary: Allbirds is reported to have pivoted from footwear to AI servers after securing $50M in funding, which sparked a large stock rally. The headlines are undated and the article body wasn't retrieved, so the details are unverified.
A Proactive headline says Allbirds secured $50M in funding tied to the AI-server pivot. Investors, terms and date are not confirmed.

Allbirds, rebranded as Smartbird, appointed Nadia Carlsten as CEO and board member, replacing Joe Vernachio. A separate snippet says the company officially changed its corporate name and named a new CEO about 8 days before the snippet was captured.
Former Allbirds CEO Joe Vernachio has been named president of Sorel. The snippet only says '5 days ago' and gives no date.

Q2 2026 results were reported on Aug 18, 2026. Revenue was $2.76M against a consensus of about $29.5M, and EPS was -$1.39 (adjusted) or -$1.79 (GAAP). The tiny revenue figure suggests the footwear business has shrunk or been divested, but that is not confirmed.
The stock is volatile: it rose 33.7% on Oct 1, 2026 to about $3.49, then fell to about $2.36 by Oct 14. The next earnings date is estimated for around Nov 5, 2026.

answer.notes: The company appears to be in a major transformation: a rebrand to Smartbird, a new CEO (Nadia Carlsten) and an AI-infrastructure pivot with reported $50M funding. This is likely a very different business from the footwear brand the seller may expect. Several key items (pivot, funding, rebrand, CEO change) come from undated snippets or headlines, so I could not confirm exact dates or details. I also did not confirm whether the footwear brand was sold or wound down, and I found no hiring, partnership or layoff signals. Before outreach, verify these items in the company's press releases or SEC filings (8-Ks), and tailor the pitch to the new AI/compute strategy rather than to footwear or DTC retail. The FourWeekMBA and Enrich Labs pages are generic and may be outdated, so I did not use them as signals.
